entry.title: The Four-Color Theorem Gets a Rare New Proof
entry.content: By revisiting the famous problem — which was controversially solved in the 1970s with the help of computers — mathematicians have gained important new insights into the nature of graphs.

entry.title: Live from ICM 2026: What Is Math For in the Age of AI?
entry.content: In this special live recording from the International Congress of Mathematicians in Philadelphia, July 2026, the central question discussed was what do mathematicians really value about doing mathematics in the first place?

entry.title: Does Computer Science Need Computers?
entry.content: The theoretical side of the field doesn’t require computing machines. But many questions would never have been posed without them.

entry.title: Are We Thinking Correctly About AI Intelligence?
entry.content: Computer scientist Melanie Mitchell discusses why artificial intelligence doesn’t “think” or “reason” like humans, and how we can create better methods for measuring machine cognition.

entry.title: Is AI Reasoning Right for the Wrong Reasons?
entry.content: The idea that artificial intelligence can “reason” is more intuitive than ever. But intuitions can be wrong, and the science is far from settled.

entry.title: A Master of the Traveling Salesperson Problem Finds His Own Path
entry.content: Shayan Oveis Gharan has won the Abacus Medal for using tools from across mathematics to boost the power of algorithms.

entry.title: Researchers Reveal the Power of ‘Quantum Proofs’
entry.content: When checking that solutions to certain problems are correct, it turns out, you can’t get around the inherent complexity of the quantum world.

entry.title: Key Chemistry Question Answered, No Quantum Computer Required
entry.content: Do we need quantum computers to fully understand complex chemical reactions? A new result, decades in the making, shows the surprising power of ordinary “classical” machines.
